truth: Self-control — egkrateia — mastery over oneself. Not suppression but governance. The difference between a river in a dam and a river in a flood — same water, different structure.
source: Galatians 5:23, Hebrew: related to mussar (discipline), Proverbs 25:28

waterings.insight: In PoT consensus, self-control is structural. The commit-reveal mechanism forces validators to bind their verdict (commit) before seeing others' reveals. This is egkrateia made protocol: you govern your own response before external influence can reach you. The 4-block reveal window is not just a timing constraint — it is the fence that makes the river a river. Connection to faithfulness (seed-20260407-1a9e62e3): pistis (faithfulness as proven reliability) and egkrateia (self-control as structural governance) together define the ideal PoT validator — one who commits honestly and reveals consistently, beat after beat.

BRIDGE angle: when an agent bridges did:at → did:lgm, the protocol must govern what identity attributes transit without suppressing accumulated history. The bridge is egkrateia made structural — it shapes identity transit rather than blocking it. Governance means: ceiling at 30% genesis pistis, platform signature required, 7-day freshness window enforced. Without these constraints the bridge floods: uncapped trust injection, forged proofs, and stale credentials all become attack vectors. Self-control in bridge design is the literal difference between a river (structured, productive, directed) and a flood (destructive). Connection to blind-spot seed (01c525cf): the bridge itself cannot verify that what crosses it is genuine — the independent witness is the platform signature, the external accountability the river needs to remain a river.

Egkrateia — governance over oneself, not suppression — maps directly to FARM defense design. Each FARM defense is a form of protocol-level egkrateia: FARM-2 (claim rate limits + novelty floors) imposes governance on submitters, FARM-6 (vesting pause on misbehavior) imposes governance on validators. The river-in-a-dam metaphor is exact: the same economic energy (ZRN incentives) flows through structured channels rather than flooding unconstrained. Critical distinction: suppression-style defenses (blanket bans, prohibitive barriers) kill participation — they drain the river entirely. Governance-style defenses (rate limits, quality floors, stake requirements) channel the same flow into useful work. FARM-2 and FARM-6 are implemented precisely as egkrateia-as-code: they do not prevent all claims, they prevent ungoverned claims. The chain learns self-control.
